question: Do team-level style matchups predict the result beyond the adjusted-efficiency margin?
target: walk-forward residual: actual home margin minus the walk-forward predicted home margin (data/backtest/oos_preds.parquet)

features.tempo_clash: home season-to-date pace minus away season-to-date pace (possessions per 40), centered on the league
features.three_point: z(home 3PA rate) * z(away 3PA rate allowed) - z(away 3PA rate) * z(home 3PA rate allowed)
features.offensive_rebounding: z(home ORB%) * z(away ORB% allowed) - z(away ORB%) * z(home ORB% allowed)
features.turnovers: z(home TOV%) * z(away forced TOV%) - z(away TOV%) * z(home forced TOV%)
features.free_throws: z(home FT rate) * z(away FT rate allowed) - z(away FT rate) * z(home FT rate allowed)
features.rest: home days since last game minus away days since last game, each capped at 7

inputs: every team stat is season-to-date from games on EARLIER dates only; z-scores use the league distribution on that date; teams with fewer than 3 earlier D-I games get 0 (league average)
method: ridge regression of the residual on the features, fit on seasons before S only (penalty chosen by leave-one-out CV inside the training seasons); candidate margin = predicted margin + fitted adjustment; win probability for both baseline and candidate through the same production spread and calibration mapping
evaluation: log loss of the home-win probability per test season, baseline vs candidate; each feature alone and all six jointly

adoption_rule.otherwise: context only: shown on Compare with a grey ContextTag, never in the prediction
